DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 7 requires every SAP record file to contain 'Written approval by SecDef or DepSecDef of carve-out status when DSS is relieved of industrial security oversight responsibilities' and 'The identification of SAP facilities ... that have been carved-out based upon this authority'. Neither the number of carve-outs in force, nor the list of carved-out facilities, nor the identity of any approving official for any individual carve-out has ever been published or FOIA-released.

The identity of the current Director of DoD SAPCO and the office's organisational chart, staffing and budget. DoDD 5205.07 requires the Director to be a general officer, flag officer or SES appointed by and reporting to the Deputy Secretary of Defense. No DoD SAPCO director has ever appeared before a public congressional hearing and the incumbent's name is not published.

The DoD Manual 5205.07 Volumes 2, 3 and 4 (Personnel Security, Physical Security, Marking). As of 12 August 2026 the esd.whs.mil URLs for all four volumes do not return the documents to ordinary public retrieval; only Volume 1 was recoverable, from an Internet Archive capture dated 18 October 2019. Volume 4 (Marking) in particular would document the DoD counterpart to the CAPCO marking rules for SAP material.

The exact signature date and signer of the reissued ICD 906. The released PDF was generated on 19 December 2024 and states that it supersedes the ICD 906 signed 17 October 2015, but the signature block in the released scan is an image that does not resolve to text.

The classified addenda to the IC Authorized Classification and Control Markings Register. The public register states on its title page that 'Certain security markings were removed due to classified content. These markings have been compiled in separate classified addenda.' The existence of compartment markings that appear in no public authority is documented; their number and identity are not.

The 50 U.S.C. 3348 reports. Every federal agency other than DoD, NNSA and the IC that runs a special access program owes an annual February 1 report to congressional oversight committees expressly including the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform. No such report from any agency has been publicly identified, and no public record shows House Oversight invoking this entitlement in the UAP context.

The section 7606(c) reports required by the FY2024 Intelligence Authorization Act. Each of the six officials authorised by E.O. 13526 to establish special access programs was required, by 22 December 2024, to report to nine congressional committees on the number of personnel eligible for SAP access and how it would be held to the minimum. No such report has surfaced publicly. Whether they were filed is answerable by a single letter from any of the nine committees.

Whether any waiver under 10 U.S.C. 119(e) has ever been exercised in connection with a UAP-related program, and whether the funding prohibitions of FY2024 NDAA section 1687 and FY2024 IAA section 7343 have ever been triggered, complied with, or certified against. Neither the Secretary of Defense nor the Director of National Intelligence has publicly stated whether any disclosure was made under either section.

GAO and DoD Inspector General coverage of the SAP enterprise. The only located GAO product touching contractor industrial security, GAO-04-332, expressly excluded special access programs from its scope by agreement with committee staff. No GAO product in the govinfo GAOREPORTS collection was located that audits DoD SAP congressional reporting, carve-out administration, or the waived-program list. Whether classified GAO or DoD IG products on these subjects exist, and under what report numbers, is unresolved.

The current DoD SAPCO-held count of SAP facilities (SAPFs) and of contractor SAPFs. DoDI 5205.11 requires the identification of carved-out facilities to be maintained; the total inventory of accredited SAP facilities has never been published even in aggregate.

The Prospective SAP (PSAP) register. DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 6 shows that a program can operate as a PSAP with enhanced security measures approved before it is ever approved as a SAP, on a 180-day path to a Deputy Secretary decision. Programs that were terminated as PSAPs before approval - as KONA BLUE was at DHS - never appear in any SAP report to Congress at all. No register of PSAPs initiated and terminated has ever been released.

Names of individuals holding SAPOC and Senior Review Group seats at any given date. The seats are defined by position in DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 3, so the membership on any past date is reconstructible from public appointment records, but no such reconstruction exists on this board and it would identify precisely who was in the room when any given program was approved.

ALIAS PAIRS REQUIRING MERGE, NOT DELETION. Five domain ids in the wave-1 corpus are near-synonyms of others and were defined here so no edge dangles, but a merge pass should decide a canonical for each: d-legislative / d-legislation (process vs enacted text); d-funding / d-money (channel vs opacity); d-secrecy / d-secrecy-architecture (law vs compartment topology); d-contractor / d-contracting (custody vs acquisition mechanics); d-ffrdc / d-ffrdc-mechanism (institution vs FAR 35.017 clause). Each pair is written here with a deliberate division of labour so both can survive if the board prefers granularity.

FOUR DOMAIN IDS WERE ALREADY DEFINED ELSEWHERE AND WERE NOT REDEFINED HERE: d-ffrdc and d-structure and d-media (in media-structure.json and ffrdcs.json) and d-custody (in scientists-technical.json). d-materials WAS redefined here because it appears in the required list; scientists-technical.json also carries a definition and the two must be reconciled rather than both loaded. Note also that media-structure.json defines a domain with the bare id 'ffrdc-mechanism' while one record references 'd-ffrdc-mechanism' - a prefix inconsistency the merge pass should normalise.

NINE DOMAINS ARE DEFINED FORWARD, NOT BACKWARD. d-intel, d-nuc, d-plasma, d-chem, d-consciousness, d-remote-viewing, d-signals, d-aerospace and d-counterintel are not yet referenced by any wave-1 person record. They were in the required list and are defined here for wave-2 and wave-3 scoring. Until people are scored on them they carry no graph weight, and a later pass should backfill domains[] on existing person records - the aviators dossier in particular should almost certainly carry d-signals, and the scientists dossier d-chem and d-astro.

THE C AXIS IS UNDER-EVIDENCED ON EXACTLY THE DOMAINS THAT MATTER MOST. d-legacy, d-recovery, d-reverse-engineering and d-bio are scored C3 on the strength of sworn testimony (tier 2) rather than primary documents (tier 1). That is honest grading, not a defect, but it means the board's central claim currently rests on one hearing. The research that would change this is contract and facility-clearance data, not more testimony.

NO PRIMARY DOCUMENT HAS BEEN LOCATED FOR THE FUNDING DOMAIN'S CENTRAL CLAIM. d-funding and d-money describe channels that demonstrably exist - transfer authority, MIPRs, IRAD, 50 U.S.C. 3510 unvouchered expenditure - and an audit failure that demonstrably exists. What is missing is any document connecting a specific dollar to a specific concealed activity. Until that exists the funding argument establishes possibility, not fact, and the dossiers say so.

SKIDMORE'S FIGURES ARE CITED AS GROSS ADJUSTMENTS, NOT MISSING MONEY, AND THE DISTINCTION IS LOAD-BEARING. The d-money dossier states this explicitly because conflating the two is the fastest way to lose the argument. A dedicated pass should locate Skidmore's published papers directly rather than relying on the DoD OIG findings that underpin them; no direct citation to his work was verified for this file.

TWO ROSWELL AIR FORCE REPORTS ARE CITED BY TITLE WITH DATING UNCERTAINTY. 'The Roswell Report: Fact vs. Fiction in the New Mexico Desert' is variously dated 1994 and 1995 across sources in the corpus; the DTIC copy cited here is dated 1995. 'The Roswell Report: Case Closed' is firmly 24 June 1997. A records pass should pin the first date to a publication record.

THE COMETA REPORT IS DESCRIBED IN THE l-paris AND l-france DOSSIERS WITHOUT A VERIFIED URL. The 1999 French report 'Les OVNI et la Defense' is real and well attested but no authoritative online copy was verified during this pass, so it appears in prose rather than in claims[] or sources[]. It should be sourced properly before any claim is built on it.

FIFTY-FOUR LOCATION IDS WERE DANGLING ACROSS THE CORPUS AND ARE NOW DEFINED, BUT TWENTY OF THEM ARE THIN BY DESIGN. The congressional home-district anchors (l-tompkinsville, l-glenbeulah, l-oro-valley and the rest) carry accurate but minimal dossiers deliberately: committee assignments and hearing roles belong on the person records in congress-house.json, and duplicating them here would create two places to get them wrong. Where a member's specific committee role could not be verified in this pass, the dossier says 'in the period covered by this board's congressional dossier' rather than asserting a role.

THREE LOCATION IDS ARE PURE ALIASES AND SHOULD BE COLLAPSED: l-washington-dc into l-dc (142 inbound references versus 2), l-lasvegas into l-las-vegas, and l-cambridge-ma into l-cambridge. They are defined here only so that no edge dangles before the merge pass runs.

THE d-consciousness DOSSIER IS THE BOARD'S WEAKEST AND IS TIERED C DELIBERATELY. Its only tier-1 content is that the government funded Star Gate for twenty-three years and commissioned Kit Green's DIRD on neurological field effects. The substantive claim - that observation is coupled to the phenomenon - has no primary support and is recorded as a tier-3 personnel-continuity inference. If the board wants to argue it, that argument has to be built from somewhere other than this file.

NO DOMAIN-LEVEL SCORING RUBRIC IS PUBLISHED. Each domain dossier explains what a high score means for that domain in prose, but there is no cross-domain calibration table, so a C3 on d-materials and a C3 on d-bio are not guaranteed to mean the same distance from custody. A calibration pass across all fifty domains would make the axis scores comparable; until then they are ordinal within a domain and only roughly comparable across domains.

AARO's VOLUME II HISTORICAL RECORD REPORT WAS NOT LOCATED IN THIS PASS. Volume I (February 2024) is cited throughout. NDAA FY2025 Section 6802 sunsets the audit requirements attached to the historical record report, which suggests the reporting obligation's status changed after 2024; the current state of Volume II and of the sunset's effect should be established directly from AARO and from P.L. 118-159's full text before any claim is made about it.
